RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

An all-female panel is common in education and is not evidence of bias. Raising the panel's gender composition will appear unprofessional, lacks legal standing, and will severely damage your credibility.

While your administrative credentials appear stronger on paper, hiring decisions frequently hinge on interview performance, references, leadership vision, and institutional fit rather than sex. Unconscious bias is always possible, but qualification differences alone do not prove it.

Do not mention the panel's gender. Instead, follow up politely on your request for written feedback. If you decide to pursue a formal inquiry or appeal, focus entirely on objective qualifications, stated selection criteria, and procedural fairness.
